newsitem.title: USA: Four killed, one wounded on ship on Miami River.
newsitem.headline: Four killed, one wounded on ship on Miami River.

text.p: Four crew members were killed and man was seriously wounded on Monday in a pre-dawn shooting aboard a coastal freighter docked on the Miami River, police said.

The bodies of three men and a woman were found early in the morning after a dockworker summoned police to a riverside neighbourhood where the Belize-registered Vanderpool Express had docked on Saturday after coming from Haiti, police said.

The congested Miami River, which flows into the heart of downtown Miami, is a port of entry for dozens of ageing freighters that ply the waters between the United States and Haiti, taking bicycles, beds, used appliances and rice to the impoverished Caribbean nation.
The crowded wharfs along the river have also been used by South American drug traffickers to unload cocaine and marijuana and by Caribbean immigrant smugglers to unload human cargo.
One body was found on deck. The other three were below deck, police said. Investigators were not immediately able to determine how the four were killed.
"The scene is so messy at this point that it's hard to determine what exactly happened," Metro-Dade Police spokeswoman Nelda Fonticiella said.
Gunshots rang out before dawn -- not an unusual occurance in the neighbourhood of houses, trailers and marine-related businesses.
"I just heard four shots. I was half asleep," longtime resident Walt Frost, said. "It happens in this area day and night -- but not that early."
An apparent survivor of the crime was taken to hospital suffering what police described as serious injuries. One television station reported the man suffered knife wounds.
Fonticiella said the wounded man, who was reported in critical condition, made a telephone call from the hospital to the dockworker, who then called police.
Investigators said it was uncertain whether the 160-foot (53-metres) freighter had come to pick up or unload cargo.
The identities of the victims, who were all apparently from the Caribbean, were not released. Police said they had no immediate indication of drug involvement in the slayings.
Residents said drug trafficking, cargo and immigrant smuggling and violence were common along the river, home to construction and metal recycling businesses, freight companies, boatyards and bars.
